name: River Okonkwo (fictional example)
introduction: A fictional demonstration profile. River is not a real person; this entry exists only to show how a Legacy profile looks.
story:
River learned to fix things in a repair shop that smelled of solder and rain. Nothing there was ever thrown away before someone had argued with it for an afternoon.

Later River wrote small tools for a neighbourhood library: a catalogue that ran on an old laptop, a sign-up sheet for reading nights, a script that reminded volunteers to lock the back door. None of it was famous. All of it was used.

River liked explaining things more than building them, and kept a notebook of the questions people were embarrassed to ask out loud.
carryForward: Fix one small thing for someone who did not ask, and write down how you did it so the next person does not have to guess.

work.title: Library catalogue (example)
work.description: A fictional example entry showing how to describe something you made and why it mattered.

work.title: Notebook of embarrassing questions (example)
work.description: A fictional collection of plain-language answers to questions people were afraid to ask.

memories: Reading nights ran late every winter, and nobody ever admitted to being the last one out.
A soldering iron with tape on the handle that outlasted three laptops.
